**Individuation** — what makes something one thing, and the same thing over time or across descriptions — individuation, numerical identity and diversity, individuality and persistence of things of any kind, biological individuality and organisational closure. Selves are self and persons are personhood (group: philosophy; ADR-015, ADR-024).

| [THEORY-066](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-066.md) | Markov blankets exist around almost any set | The formal core of Bruineberg et al.'s critique ([LIT-603](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-603.md), C4 in [NOTE-447](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-447.md)). In a directed acyclic graph the blanket of a node set A is its parents, children and the children's other parents, and A is conditionally independent of everything outside A and its blanket. That holds for every A, so any set whose blanket leaves something outside gets a valid internal, blanket and external partition. Having a blanket therefore picks out no set. In Friston's soup ([LIT-526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-526.md)) the set was picked by spectral clustering with k = 8, not by the blanket. Active because it is a short derivation that anyone can check. It covers graphical (Pearl) blankets and the 2013 procedure. It does not cover the later sparse-coupling definitions at nonequilibrium steady state, which the record has not read. | Active |
| [THEORY-071](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-071.md) v3 | Individuality alone is not agency | Barandiaran, Di Paolo & Rohde (2009), [LIT-566](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-566.md), read in [NOTE-458](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-458.md). The three conditions are that the system distinguishes itself from its environment with no observer doing it, that it is the active source of modulations of its coupling with the environment, and that it regulates that coupling against norms its own organisation sets. Each is necessary, and together they are claimed to be sufficient. Individuality is the precondition of the other two and does not suffice. A cell in passive osmosis, a kitten warmed by its mother and a person with a Parkinsonian tremor are each individuals, and none of them is acting. The generative definition is an open autonomous organisation that adaptively modulates its coupling so as to maintain itself. Here "autonomy" and "self" mean organisational closure. They do not mean a subject or self-governance. Proposed: a conceptual analysis checked against intuitive cases, with an asymmetry criterion its authors call incomplete. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-072](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md) v5 | Organisms differ from flames by differentiation | The record's first answer to the demarcation question that [NOTE-094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-094.md) reports. Mossio, Saborido & Moreno (2009, [LIT-570](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-570.md)) grant a candle flame organisational closure. Its one macroscopic pattern keeps up the conditions of the combustion that makes it. They draw the line at organisational differentiation: in an organism several distinct structures make distinct contributions, where a flame makes "a unique contribution". Montévil & Mossio (2015, [LIT-582](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-582.md)) narrow closure to mutual dependence among constraints. Each constraint must be both produced by and productive of another, with at least one slow and one fast dependence. On the record's reading, that builds differentiation into closure, as Mossio and Bich (2014) already say of closure of constraints. No paper analyses a flame under the 2015 definitions. Neither paper says closure defines an organism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-073](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-073.md) v3 | Blanket placement is fixed by prior modelling | Bruineberg et al. ([LIT-603](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-603.md)) and Raja et al. | [THEORY-221](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-221.md) v2 | Organizational closure differs from feedback | Rubin, Roli, Stano & Damiano (2026), [LIT-1027](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1027.md), read in [NOTE-727](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-727.md). A genealogy of closure notions from logic, cybernetics, systems theory, thermodynamics, relational biology and the biology of cognition, and an interpretive thesis drawn from it. The genealogy shows that "closure" names different things (information, operations, efficient causes, constraints, catalysts). | [THEORY-265](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-265.md) v3 | Module-matched synchrony makes modules units | Tissot, Levin, Buckley & Watson (2024), [LIT-989](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-989.md), read in full (v1 and v2) in [NOTE-773](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-773.md). In a simulated game of 30 modules of 10 units, each unit shifts the phase of its decision cycle toward partners it currently agrees with. Phases synchronise within modules, each module then switches as a block, and 50 of 50 runs with the learned phases reach a global optimum against 0 of 50 without; imposed global synchrony does not help. It is one clean game, one parameter setting, and a postulated phase rule; the modules are built in, and timing finds them rather than drawing them. Re-implemented by the sixteenth status review: learned phases, and module-matched phases imposed by hand, reach the optimum; random, shuffled and global phases do not make modules respond as units. The effect matters only where modules are isolated enough to lock in. | Active |

| [THEORY-452](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-452.md) | Supervaluation and near-identity count one cat | Lewis (1993), [LIT-1015](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1015.md), read in full in [NOTE-722](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-722.md). Two answers to Unger's problem of the many, offered together. Supervaluation makes "there is one cat" super-true at the granted cost that nothing is super-truly the cat. Almost-identity, which is overlap and not similarity, makes the many candidates "almost one". It is not transitive and its threshold is left undecided. Each covers a case the other fails: Fred's house needs supervaluation, and supervaluation is natural only where the candidates differ little. It assumes semantic indecision, perdurance and no natural joint among the candidates. It has no metric, no dynamics and no threshold, so it is a precedent for counting by something weaker than identity, not evidence for any of the record's claims. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-453](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-453.md) | Physical objects can be mere relation-bearers | Esfeld & Lam (2008), [LIT-895](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-895.md), read in full in [NOTE-695](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-695.md). Moderate structural realism: relations require relata, but relata need no fundamental intrinsic properties, and objects and relations depend on each other with no priority. Its distinctive move is primitive numerical diversity, which it says gives no identity of any sort. The GR sections show interpretive fit, not entailment. Identity is equivocal between §1, where symmetric space-times need primitive diversity, and §2, where the metric "completely determines" structural identity; the one concrete construction cited works only without symmetries and breaks the general covariance the view rests on. The no-priority argument assumes three options are exhaustive. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-535](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-535.md) | Quasi-sets count indistinguishable particles | Holik, Jorge, Krause & Lombardi (2021), [LIT-107](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-107.md), read in full from the preprint in [NOTE-127](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-127.md). | [THEORY-546](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-546.md) v2 | Persons persist by psychological continuity | Locke (1694), [LIT-464](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-464.md), read in [NOTE-385](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-385.md), with the repairs as Olson's survey ([LIT-454](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-454.md), [NOTE-374](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-374.md)) and Parfit ([LIT-447](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-447.md), [NOTE-378](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-378.md)) give them. | [THEORY-575](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-575.md) | Social groups are two kinds of thing | Ritchie (2020, online 2018), [LIT-486](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-486.md), read in [NOTE-389](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-389.md), building on her 2013 view ([LIT-479](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-479.md)). | [THEORY-579](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-579.md) v2 | Constantly used external stores can hold beliefs | Clark & Chalmers (1998), [LIT-097](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-097.md), read in [NOTE-180](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-180.md), with Clark's reply to the critics (2005), [LIT-403](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-403.md), read in [NOTE-363](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-363.md). | [THEORY-622](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-622.md) | Wholes of separate bodies are fiat objects | Smith & Varzi (2000), [LIT-1024](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1024.md), read in full in [NOTE-721](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-721.md). The test is whether a discontinuity is there, not who or what made it. The theory is spatial, synchronic and pitched at the common-sense level; it has no models or consistency result, and the typology is stipulated by examples. It does not map onto the record's produced/imposed distinction, and it classifies the record's combined forms as fiat without choosing among them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-650](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-650.md) | Diachronic self-identity is level-relative | Floridi (2011), [LIT-136](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-136.md), read in [NOTE-130](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-130.md). The deflation of diachronic identity is an informal argument from examples that rests on the method of levels of abstraction, assumed from elsewhere; that this "is not relativism" is one sentence, and that individuation comes before identification is asserted. It is not, as its title suggests, a criterion of personal identity, and its positive answer to the synchronic question, the three-membranes model, is "somewhat figurative" by its author's word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-666](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-666.md) | Autopoiesis gives organisms intrinsic purpose | Weber & Varela (2002), [LIT-1018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1018.md), read in full in [NOTE-720](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-720.md). An essay of exegesis and convergence: Kant's natural purposes read non-reductively, Jonas's metabolism-based philosophy of the organism, and autopoiesis. The step from self-production to purpose is asserted ("Bluntly stated"), the step to subjectivity is Jonas's phenomenological inversion, and no observable is proposed for the "empirical feature" the conclusion claims. What sets autopoiesis apart from dissipative structures is placed in "concern", not in organisation. One paragraph runs from self-maintenance to a right to life. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1050](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1050.md) v2 | Dependence-first bias rests on one mapping | Athreya, Czuppon & Gokhale (2025), [LIT-1570](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1570.md), read in [NOTE-1211](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1211.md). In the exponential version of the model, all four traits rise monotonically. Each partner becomes more obligate than adhesive, because a gain in adhesion is "damped by the other adhesion" in the dissociation rate. Table S1 shows this is a consequence of that mapping: matched mappings give no bias, and the opposite mapping biases trajectories towards cohesion. The record's summary of the result, "even when investments are uncorrelated", is true of the traits' genetic correlation but not of their functional coupling, which is what decides it. | Active |
| [THEORY-1051](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1051.md) v3 | Mutual dependence is parameter-bound, not default | Athreya, Czuppon & Gokhale (2025), [LIT-1570](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1570.md), read in [NOTE-1211](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1211.md). With the symbiont's population larger and faster, its obligacy reaches 1 first. In the base model the host's R₀ is then exactly 1, so host obligacy is neutral. With within-collective deaths the host goes fully obligate, and with within-collective births it goes back to independence. Obligacy rose from zero in simulations where the collective's carrying capacity exceeded about aK_HK_S/d, a condition shown sufficient, not necessary; collective growth rate does not matter. The authors take the model as a null: a transition "is far from an inevitable outcome of the existence of a higher level of selection". | Active |
| [THEORY-1097](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1097.md) | No Markov blanket formulation individuates | The wider claim dropped when [THEORY-073](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-073.md) was narrowed to Friston's 2013 formulation and promoted on 2026-10-27 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4: a narrowing's dropped claims go to Proposed entries). Both critiques argue the general form, and the record holds neither of the later formulations it would have to reach. Its promote_when is [THEORY-073](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-073.md)'s own, moved here unchanged. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1107.md) v2 | Organelles arise stepwise via protein import | Sørensen, Stiller, Kröninger & Nowack (2025), [LIT-1560](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1560.md), read in [NOTE-1241](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1241.md). Their closing scenario orders the steps from endosymbiont to organelle: effectors first, then dependence through one redundant imported protein, then many imported proteins once a targeting signal evolves. Rhizobia, targeted by about 700 host peptides yet not vertically transmitted, are their case of control without integration. It is a scenario built from systems at different stages, not a sequence observed in any one. | Active |
| [THEORY-1119](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1119.md) v3 | Minimal agency needs three sufficient marks | What the paper proposes, split from [THEORY-071](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-071.md) by the tenth status review on [THEORY-1110](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1110.md)'s pattern, so that claims needing only the proposal can stand on it. The paper was read in full ([NOTE-458](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-458.md)), so the reading of what it proposes is held. Whether the definition is right, which turns on an asymmetry criterion its authors call incomplete and on applying the conditions to explicit models, stays [THEORY-071](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-071.md)'s question, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-1163](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1163.md) v2 | Information individuality favours largest boundary | Krakauer, Bertschinger, Olbrich, Flack and Ay (2020), [LIT-1137](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1137.md), read in [NOTE-1400](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1400.md). Mutual information cannot fall when either argument is enlarged, and A′ ≥ A follows by the chain rule with the remaining environment as condition. It is a fact about the measures, not about any system. It does not say how to price size, and nC, the third measure, can move either way. It is the formal content of A11's remark recorded in [QUESTION-115](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-115.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1194](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1194.md) v2 | Coupled external stores can carry beliefs | What the extended-mind paper argues, split from [THEORY-579](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-579.md) by the sixteenth status review on [THEORY-1110](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1110.md)'s pattern ([ADR-058](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-058.md)'s route), so that [CLAIM-175](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-175.md), which argues "on the extended-mind thesis's own terms", can stand on the statement of those terms. Both papers were read in full ([NOTE-180](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-180.md), [NOTE-363](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-363.md)), and Clark (2005) says in his own words that the parity principle was not argued. Whether the conditional holds, that coupling of this kind makes a store part of a mind, stays [THEORY-579](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-579.md)'s question, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-1211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1211.md) | Endosymbionts become organelles in steps | The wider thesis Sørensen, Stiller, Kröninger & Nowack assert, filed beside [THEORY-1107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1107.md) by the twenty-second status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1107.md), Active, holds the scenario Sørensen and colleagues propose; whether the thesis holds is this entry's question, and its promote_when is [THEORY-1107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1107.md)'s old condition, word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1243](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1243.md) | Endosymbiotic dependence precedes cohesion | The inference Athreya, Czuppon and Gokhale draw for nature, filed beside [THEORY-1050](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1050.md) by the twenty-fourth status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1050](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1050.md), Active, holds the model result and its dependence on the trait mapping; whether real symbioses are dependence-first is this entry's question, with [THEORY-1050](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1050.md)'s old condition. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1247](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1247.md) | Collaboration marks a new level of individuality | What Griesemer and Shavit's sketch proposes. The twenty-fourth status review split it from [THEORY-418](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-418.md) ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3), so that the record holds the reading of the proposal apart from the proposal. The paper was read in full ([NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md)), so the reading is held. Whether the proposal is right is [THEORY-418](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-418.md), Proposed, which extends this entry. That needs criteria that sort real groups into the three grades, and worked cases. The paper's two headline claims, non-circularity and individuality as a special case of collectivity, are in its abstract only and are not part of this entry. | Active |
| [THEORY-1276](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1276.md) v2 | Information is disparity, meaning is transduction | Iliadis (2013), [LIT-1911](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1911.md), read in [NOTE-1485](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1485.md), with Bencherki & Iliadis (2021), [LIT-1922](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1922.md). The reading of Simondon on which Bencherki, Brummans & Vézy (2024) build their account of communication and meaning. Active as a report of how the two read him: both sources are exegesis in their authors' translations, and whether Simondon holds this, which turns on his own text, is THEORY-1534's question, Proposed. It does not say that information has no quantitative sense, or that meaning can be identified before the resolution occurs. | Active |
| [THEORY-1277](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1277.md) | Persons and organizations are coexisting levels | Bencherki & Iliadis (2021), [LIT-1922](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1922.md), read in [NOTE-1483](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1483.md), with Bencherki (2017), [LIT-1901](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1901.md). The claim behind the parent paper's dissolution of the scaling-up problem ([LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), p. 1364). Proposed: a conceptual proposal, illustrated by one meeting excerpt, with no criterion that fixes a level independently of the analyst. It redescribes the problem; it does not show that aggregation never occurs. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1278.md) | Communication is transduction, not exchange | Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy (2024), [LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), read in [NOTE-1484](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1484.md), pp. 1355–1358 and 1363–1365. Simondon's transduction made into a theory of organizational communication. Proposed: argued from examples, with the dissolution of scaling up asserted. The examples (a synapse, a hunger pang, a piston) show the notion applies to any change, which is its strength as a vocabulary and its weakness as a theory. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1280](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1280.md) | Agency is affective force, agents its effects | Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy (2024), [LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), read in [NOTE-1484](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1484.md), pp. 1349–1357. The paper's central proposal, after the Spinozan formula for affect that Massumi offers as a proposition, not a definition, and Simondon's individuation. Proposed: argued, and illustrated by one reanalysed meeting. It has no criterion that would let an observation count against it, and it builds the augmenting direction into the definition of agency. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1285.md) | Whose action it is results from individuation | Bencherki (2017), [LIT-1901](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1901.md), read in [NOTE-1482](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1482.md), with Bencherki & Iliadis (2021), [LIT-1922](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1922.md). The proposal of which Bencherki, Brummans & Vézy's "agency without agents" ([LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md)) is a development. Proposed: argued, and illustrated by three excerpts from one documentary. Nothing identifies disindividuation apart from the affect it is inferred from, and the account needs, but disclaims, a standard of whose action it rightly was. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1351](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1351.md) v2 | Shared interests, not policing, drive transitions | West et al. (2015), [LIT-2003](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2003.md), read in [NOTE-1538](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1538.md). A colloquium review: the definition and the two steps are the authors' framework, and the explanatory claim is drawn from the comparative literature they cite. Proposed because they call it "tentative", and because the theory for transitions between species is missing on their own account. It differs from [THEORY-141](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-141.md) on mechanism: group formation, not policing, does the work. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1531](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1531.md) | Communication as transduction dissolves scaling | What Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy (2024) propose, read in full in [NOTE-1484](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1484.md) (pp. 1355–1358, 1363–1365), split from [THEORY-1278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1278.md) by the twenty-seventh status review on [THEORY-1110](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1110.md)'s pattern ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md)). The dissolution of scaling up is asserted, with the MSF meeting as illustration. Whether treating communication this way changes any verdict stays [THEORY-1278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1278.md)'s question, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-1534](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1534.md) v2 | Information is disparity, not a signal | The wide form of the reading in [THEORY-1276](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1276.md), kept when the twenty-seventh status review promoted that entry as a report ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). Iliadis (2013) and Bencherki & Iliadis (2021) assert that this is Simondon's view. Whether it is turns on his own text, which the record holds only as Unavailable ([LIT-1648](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1648.md), [LIT-1900](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1900.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1535](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1535.md) | Persons and organizations coexist as levels | What Bencherki & Iliadis (2021) propose, read in full in [NOTE-1483](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1483.md) from the authors' manuscript, split from [THEORY-1277](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1277.md) by the twenty-seventh status review on [THEORY-1110](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1110.md)'s pattern ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md)), so that a claim needing only the proposal can stand on it. Whether the description discriminates from a scaling-up account stays [THEORY-1277](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1277.md)'s question, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-1564](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1564.md) v2 | Know an entity through its individuation | Bencherki and Iliadis (2019), [LIT-1922](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1922.md), read in [NOTE-1483](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1483.md) from the authors' manuscript. The fourth of the paper's four propositions (ms. pp. 21–22), stated without argument. The other readings of the paper hold its account of information, coexisting levels and meaning, not this proposition. | Active |
| [THEORY-1601](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1601.md) v2 | Planarian memory may survive decapitation | Levin and Shomrat (2013), [LIT-1776](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1776.md), read in [NOTE-1283](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1283.md) (marked Skimmed for its thinness, read in full) in place of Shomrat and Levin 2013 ([LIT-1732](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1732.md)). An automated device trained 12 worms at a time, around the clock, scored by computer, to meet the objections to McConnell's hand-run work. No numbers, methods or controls are given, and the store is said to be unknown. | Active |
| [THEORY-1607](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1607.md) v2 | Synaptic plasticity alone can't explain memory | Blackiston, Shomrat and Levin (2015), [LIT-1707](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1707.md), read in [NOTE-1258](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1258.md). A perspective with no new data. It calls the insect mechanism unsolved and the mushroom-body account indirect, and describes the lobe the 2008 moth paper relied on as partly pruned. Its non-synaptic "blueprint" and its bioelectric store are hypotheses; the planarian evidence is the authors' own one-sentence result and a contested 1960s literature. | Active |
| [THEORY-1628](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1628.md) v2 | Researchers individuate into what they study | Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy (2024), [LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), read in [NOTE-1484](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1484.md) from the version of record. A methodological demand made in one paragraph of the discussion, argued by quotation rather than for. The other readings of the paper hold its account of agency and of communication as transduction, not this demand. [NOTE-1484](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1484.md) finds it in tension with the paper's earlier treatment of the agential cut as "but an analytical choice" (p. 1357). | Active |
| [THEORY-1634](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1634.md) v2 | Caterpillar odour aversion survives metamorphosis | Blackiston, Silva Casey and Weiss (2008), [LIT-1680](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1680.md), read in [NOTE-1249](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1249.md). After fifth-instar odour-shock training, 78% of larvae (N = 41) and 77% of the moths they became (N = 27) avoided ethyl acetate, and 12 of 15 tracked individuals chose alike at both stages. Washing trained pupae or scenting naive ones changed nothing. Third-instar training survived two larval molts (81%, N = 32) and was not expressed by adults (N = 15, a null). The mushroom-body carrier is the authors' hypothesis, not tested. | Active |
| [THEORY-1654](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1654.md) | Microchimerism is bidirectional and long-lived | Chua and colleagues' consensus of 29 microchimerism researchers ([LIT-2415](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2415.md), read in [NOTE-1768](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1768.md)). The established half is what the owner's link to graded individuality needs as a premise; the open half is why it cannot yet carry more. Proposed because the established half rests on primary studies not read here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1658](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1658.md) | LysM+CD11c+ maternal cells sustain tolerance | Peng, Way and colleagues' result as Cincinnati Children's reports it ([LIT-2428](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2428.md), read in [NOTE-1763](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1763.md)). The persistence of foreign-origin cells in a host and their part in the host's regulation come apart: one marked subset does the tolerogenic work, and the rest persist without it. Proposed because the source is a press post and the paper could not be read; the Europe PMC abstract agrees with it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1691](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1691.md) | Microchimeric cells form an extended immune self | Kinder, Stelzer, Arck and Way, read in [NOTE-1728](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1728.md) (Read). A review arguing that the bidirectional transfer of cells between mother and fetus during pregnancy, and their persistence for decades (fetal cells in mothers: fetal microchimerism, FMC; maternal cells in offspring: maternal microchimerism, MMC), is not accidental but serves reproductive fitness: in mice, maternal microchimeric cells sustain offspring's regulatory T cell tolerance of non-inherited maternal antigens (NIMAs), which protects the offspring's own later pregnancies sired by NIMA-matched males (Kinder et al. 2015, ref. 14), and fetal cells retained in mothers may analogously protect later pregnancies (supported in humans by partner-specific protection against preeclampsia). Microchimeric cells may also replace injured tissue or be targets of alloimmunity resembling autoimmunity; causal roles in humans are mostly unestablished. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1718](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1718.md) | Maternal cells in fetal brain aid development | Schepanski et al., read in [NOTE-1759](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1759.md) (Read). Maternal cells (maternal microchimeric cells, MMc) transfer to the fetus and seed the fetal brain, concentrating in prefrontal cortex and hippocampus. By scRNA-seq, brain MMc are mostly microglia, plus T, B, endothelial and neuron-like cells. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2085](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2085.md) | Identity learning may proceed in phases | From the owner's unfinished proposal [LIT-2875](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2875.md), read in [NOTE-2172](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2172.md). A hypothesis, not a finding; the design to test it is [CASE-298](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-298.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2220](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2220.md) | A flame self-maintains without closure | Mossio and Moreno, read in [NOTE-2311](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2311.md) (Read). A flame is far-from-equilibrium self-maintenance through one constraint; an organism has organisational closure, a set of constraints each maintaining another that maintains it. Closure is partial, holds among constraints not processes, and is direct. It is necessary for an organism, not sufficient. A stand-in, in part, for [LIT-536](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-536.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2269](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2269.md) | Scaffolds can impose Darwinian properties first | Bourrat, Takacs, Doulcier, Nitschke, Black, Hammerschmidt and Rainey (2024), read in [NOTE-2362](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2362.md) (Read), a neighbour of [LIT-1940](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1940.md). A perspective piece: the two-peaks condition is borrowed from Doulcier et al. (2024) and the constructive route is proposed for future models. Its operative-cause definition assumes no feedback, which the constructive route is. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2270](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2270.md) | Transitions complete when scaffolds internalize | Bourrat (2022), read in [NOTE-2361](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2361.md) (Read). The criterion (§2, Table 1) grades collective properties as pseudo-Darwinian, Darwinian-like and Darwinian by the source of the mechanisms producing them; the model (§5-6) lifts one part of the scaffold, the migration ban, and leaves patches, their capacity and the periodic propagule generations in place. The author calls the result preliminary. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2271](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2271.md) | Neolithic was a transition in individuality | Shavit and Sharon (2023), read in [NOTE-2363](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2363.md) (Read). An opinion paper: the stage assignments are made by fit with a published archaeological synthesis, and the authors say they do not examine how far the case meets ETI criteria. It is the application of [LIT-188](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md)'s sketch, not a test of it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2275.md) | Reproducers develop and overlap with progeny | Wilkins and Bourrat's SEP entry (2022 revision), §5.4, read in [NOTE-2367](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2367.md) (Skimmed), a neighbour of [LIT-1932](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1932.md) and [LIT-1937](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1937.md). A survey's report of Griesemer, not Griesemer; one of its page citations points to the wrong paper. | Proposed |
